title: Angular CLI Code Generation knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Angular CLI Code Generation”?
options: Angular CLI Code Generation should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Angular CLI Code Generation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Angular CLI Code Generation means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Angular CLI Code Generation removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Angular CLI Code Generation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Angular CLI Code Generation is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Generating components” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Generating components” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Generating components” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Generating components” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Generating components” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Generating components” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Generating components” under Angular CLI Code Generation. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Angular CLI Code Generation”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
